primarySources.supports: InputStream.readAllBytes does not close its receiver; I/O failures can leave stream state inconsistent. The probe concerns the explicit no-close effect, not atomic consumption or rollback.
Closing ByteArrayInputStream has no effect on subsequent operations, so reuse after close does not establish that an enclosing consumer honored borrowed ownership.

assumptions: Case contracts explicitly distinguish caller-owned and transferred resources; this fact is supplied in the interface, not inferred from AutoCloseable.
The synthetic fixture is bounded to 64 KiB by its stated adapter; no production large-stream buffering claim is made.
The transferred application operation is distinct from an override of InputStream.readAllBytes; only the latter inherits the JDK's no-close promise.
limitations: Compilation used --release 21 and class-file major 65 was checked; runtime execution used Temurin 25.0.3+9-LTS, not a Java 21 VM.
The probes cover ordinary synchronous success/failure ownership behavior, not asynchronous close, interruption, every stream subclass, close-failure suppression or a real application.
